text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Financial holding Compagnie de Suez expects to post 1996 profit of 800 million francs, continues to clean up its real-estate portfolio.
-- Merrill Lynch chairman David Komansky says in an interview his goal is to achieve a minimum 15 percent return on equity across market cycles.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Government seeks to limit use of "Robien" law allowing payroll charge relief for firms who reduce work hours in order to keep or create jobs.
-- France and Germany seek to co-operate to avoid a competition on tax policies which is spreading across Europe.
-- AGF, Bic and Valeo to be part of blue-chip Paris bourse CAC 40 index from today.
-- Project of long-haul military transport airplane may be funded through a state-guaranteed structure receiving state funds and issuing bonds, according to project manager at Airbus Industrie.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade proposes four measures to help French banks recover.
L'AGEFI
-- Compagnie de Suez sells four billion francs worth of real estate assets to U.S. investment fund Whitehall.
-- The future of Credit Foncier de France is not certain, even if it does prove profitable.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- President Jacques Chirac launches crusade for youth employment.
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot says France must create its own labour model.
-- Talk that Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux may be considering alliance possibilities once again.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Government consiiders law forbidding certain works of art to leave the country.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- EU tensions flare over call to make taxes more uniform, end unfair competition relying on tax incentives.
LE PARISIEN
-- Judge seeks to investigate an alleged hole in Total oil group's accounts.
